title: Widespread signs of instability at TL and ALP
comment: Skinning up towards Balu Pass our AST 1 crew observed several recent (within the past 12-24hours) natural size 1-2.5 windslabs that had released out of the lower slopes off Cheops N. Bowl. We also had fairly significant whumpfing as we approached the lower slopes below Balu Pass. At a re-group in the flats below Balu Pass we watched as a rider came through some cliffs on the steeper slope lookers right of Balu Pass and triggered size 2 avalanche (Attached Photo). The individual was caught in this avalanche and was carried 10-20 metres in the debris flow before stopping on a bench mid-slope and…

title: Scoping Out The Connaught Drainage After The Storm
comment: We skinned from the parking lot which has 0-10cm on the ground. It increases dramatically once on the trail to about 40cm deep. We reliably measured 50cm at 1650m. Great travel conditions on the way up with decent coverage of the trail. The Hospital uptrack was in okay shape requiring some minor acrobatics to get over the usual obstacles. HS at TL is highly variable from 50-120cm. The alpine around Video and 8812 looks very scoured with many slopes being barely skiable. It needs another 50-100cm... Non-stop whumfing and shooting cracks at TL, more pronounced on lee features. Our group remote t…

title: Balu Pass
comment: Expected minimal snow and that’s what we got. - Balu pass skin track is in alright condition and can begin skinning not far after parking lot - Skin track follows creek side and doesn’t cross the bridge unlike last season. - Once out of the trees skin track has decent coverage. - Skied out until just after frequent flyer then transitioned. Lots of sharks still hidden away. - Found 50cm of Snow at just above 2000m. - Riding down Balu pass had soft pow but once you got just above the exit of 8812 bowl it was shallow.

title: Balu pass - skins from the lot, core shots on the way down
comment: Decent coverage on the up track besides a few spots directly under tree cover. Snow was falling sporadically and vis was in and out. Probe at the top of Balu pass reading just shy of 70cm. I tested the waters on a steeper section of the face with a stop above some rocks, my sluff from the stop quickly accumulated sending a growing but very slow moving mass of wet loose snow down in front of me. Approximately 20 meters downhill starting at a board length in width and ending 4ish meters wide. Slow moving but it accumulated quickly and continued growing until the angle mellowed out. Few sharks on…

title: A long walk with a tiny bit of skiing
comment: Had plans to go ski off of Young’s Peak but the wind at the Asulkan hut was much higher than what was forecasted. Guessing in the 40km/hr range. Was tough to stand after gusts. Noticed some wind slabs forming on Lee features and experienced shoots cracks on the last pitch before the cabin. Very typical for the feature. Wasn’t feeling like getting freezing cold and pushed around so turned around there. Wind scoured at a lot of spots above the hut. Good ski conditions once back at tree line or BTL. 60cm coverage most of the way till the last stretch of the tree triangle at about 1800m where ther…

title: Echo and Gothics Glaciers
comment: Average of 50cm HS at TL increasing to 60-80 on non glaciated alpine features. Enough snow to make for reasonable travel on skins at TL and above. On the Echo glacier we found an average of 90cm HS and then up to 160cm on the Gothics glacier. 10cm low density snow on the surface and a generally right side up snowpack above 2500m. Lower down the snowpack is facetted and weak. Saw 2 older avalanches (size 1.5 and 2) down to ice on north facing features between 2300-2500m. We skied the east facing line on Sentinel and then the Echo glacier. Ski quality was good but much more snow needed to make a…

title: Better than expected
comment: McCrae. HS @ TL ~40cm, @ toe of glacier 70cm, @ top of ridge 2220m NW asp as low as 10cm. Widespread large surface hoar sz 2-4cm. Most predominant in open sheltered BTL and in ALP. Dug a quick pit in N asp. open TL meadow to investigate layering, results in photo. Skiing on the glacier was surprisingly good! Consolidated soft snow. No signs of instability observed. Entrance and exit on the summer trail suprisingly smooth.

title: Early-Season Asulkan Assault
comment: Brought the snowshoes but managed to hike with them on my back all the way to the hut. Travel time one way was two-and-a-half hours from parking lot. Way spottier snow coming through the woods than when I did it this time last year. Ground cover gets pretty consistent past the turnoff for Great Glacier. Watch for some exposed icy sections after the turnoff for Glacier Crest and stick to the snow. Super breezy hiking and easy crossing all rivers/creeks, which are largely frozen over. Things slowed down along the final moraine climb, as soft snow deepened to as much as a foot-and-a-half. Nothing…

title: 1st day of the season!
comment: When I got out of my car, I was worried at the only other car at the parking lot had two hikers. I strapped my skis and boots to my backpack, and headed out with my hikers. Fortunately I did not have to walk for long; I quickly shifted to skinning. The Connaught creek uptrack is 95% covered, with most of the bare patches at the beginning of the route. Initially the snow coverage was minimal (1cm at the parking lot; 5cm at the beginning of the skin track), but it slowly began to accumulate. There was a surface crust buried 5cm below that disappeared around 1800m elevation. At Balu pass (2200m) …

title: Hope you like rocks, cause we’ve got heaps of f*cking rocks
comment: Went for a trundle up hermit today to see how the alpine is shaping up. Snow line is sitting around 1650m. You can still basically hike up to the campground. I ditched the trail runners after 2.5km of hiking and managed to break some kind of a trail on skins from just below 1800m. Freezing level came up disgustingly high over the weekend, precip was still falling as rain at 2000m in the afternoon. Just under 50cm of snow sitting on the tent pads at Hermit Campground but streams are still running above 2000m. Snow quality a little nicer as you get higher above the campground. Averaging 80cm of …

title: Maddysparklez Megamind Mission
comment: Up to 30cm of well consolidated snow at 1800m with 5-10cm accumulating over 24hours. Graupel & some stellar stellars overnight. Lots of wind, not much transport at our elevation. Lower elevations lost snow coverage quickly. Paw pen 5cm tested by our dawg. 10/10 would recommend an early season mission.

title: POSTPONED: Rogers Pass Gun Verification Nov 4 -7, 2026
comment: Due to incoming weather not allowing proper gunsight verification, Parks Canada has postponed this week's shoot until early next week. Updates will be posted when dates for the verification shoot are confirmed.

title: Rogers Pass Gun Verification, Nov 4-7, 2026
comment: ⚠️Important notice for Rogers Pass backcountry users! From November 4-7, 2026, the East Rogers area will be CLOSED in order for Parks Canada and the Canadian Armed Forces to test the howitzers (similar to a cannon) used for avalanche control in Rogers Pass. Intermittent closures on the Trans-Canada Highway will be required while these operations are underway. Before you travel, check DriveBC for details: https://drivebc.ca Called a verification shoot, this drill ensures the 105 mm howitzers are firing accurately to protect the highway corridor from avalanches in winter. title: Mt Rogers South Face aka Halloween suffer fest.
comment: Needed to hike to the toe of the glacier as the approach is unskinable. HS of 20cm - 65cm on various point of Swiss Glacier. Crevasses and low points/depressions are visible and manageable. Low angle glacier skiing was great, approx 10-15cm of sugary facet snow. The steep Southern face of Rogers was sun affected and crusty. Crust broke off in chucks (approx 2cm thick) but did not propagate. We switched from skinning to boot packing 1/3 of the way up. Sunny and clear conditions, alpine temps stayed below freezing during the time spent on the face. During our day we saw no signs of warming or in…

title: Kootenay Pass early season conditions
comment: Quick outing up the logging toad to Lightning Strike cabin -HS about 60cm -1cm thick rain crust about 5 cm down meant turns off-piste are challenging -not enough base for me to try much off piste -air temp at 1pm at 1900m was about 2C -worthwhile outing if you keep your expectations LOW

title: Check on Pass Conditions
comment: Had the hut booked, not enough to ski but enough to skin on the road. Tree skiing is going to need a lot more with the amount of melting going on
